verdict.rationale: ROS 2 offers building blocks for this story: QoS settings designed for non-ideal networks that range from TCP-like reliable to UDP-like best-effort delivery, local rosbag recording (CLI and a Python API that records while processing continues), and managed-lifecycle nodes. However, nothing in the evidence describes behavior when cloud connectivity drops, store-and-forward buffering to a cloud backend, or automatic clean recovery and resync, so operators would need to assemble this themselves. Missing for 10: documented offline or cloud-disconnect operation, store-and-forward upload of buffered data on reconnect, clean reconnection and recovery semantics, hands-on corroboration.
